newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal detains 1,000 people in a general strike.
newsitem.headline: Nepal detains 1,000 people in a general strike.

text.p: Nepali authorities on Friday detained about 1,000 people in a nationwide general strike called by communists to protest against a water-sharing treaty with India, party officials said.
The strike brought commercial life in the Himalayan kingdom's capital to a virtual standstill on Friday, witnesses said.
A Home (Interior) Ministry spokesman said 17 public and private vehicles were damaged and eight people wounded in stone throwing by protesters to force cars off the road at different places.
"The strike was a complete success," said the organisers, National Democratic Front Nepal (NDFN), an alliance between two communist factions.
Schools and most shops in central Kathmandu were closed, and public transport including taxis were not operating, they said.
The NDFN, opposes a proposed treaty between India and Nepal over the sharing of water from the Mahakali river on the kingdom's western border with India.
Nepal's parliament began debate on the treaty this week.
The accord aims to resolve a five-year-old bilateral dispute over the sharing of benefits from the Tanakpur dam built by India in 1991 on the Mahakali river.
The treaty spells out the terms of a new multi-billion dollar dam on the river to generate electricity and supply irrigation water.
Leftist opposition parties complain that the treaty discriminates against Nepal, which is much smaller than its populous and sprawling southern neighbour.
"A new treaty based on the principle of equality should be negotiated," an NDFN spokesman said.
